strategies.title: LP-polished adaptive basin search
strategies.plan: Retain the current variable-width SQP model, but add an exact linear-program radius polish for every candidate center set: with centers and width fixed, maximize \(\sum r_i\) subject to wall bounds and \(r_i+r_j\le d_{ij}\). This replaces potentially suboptimal SQP radii by the globally optimal radii for those centers, then uses that polished point as the next analytic-Jacobian SLSQP start. After the existing topology starts, take the best polished packing and make deterministic small, medium, and anisotropic center perturbations around it; initialize each perturbation by a conservative distance-and-wall radius construction, polish it by LP, and rerun SQP. The LP has only 21 variables and directly enforces unsquared Euclidean separation inequalities, while the final common radius shrink supplies a numerical safety margin for both wall containment and pairwise non-overlap. This is a local exploitation route with an incumbent fallback: retain the prior best whenever no polished/reoptimized candidate improves it. Expected raw radii sum is 2.36610, versus the incumbent 2.36424813084; \(2.36610/2.3658321334167627=1.0001133>0.999330467045\), so the predicted combined_score is 1.0001133.

strategies.title: Alternating boundary-interior subsystem solve
strategies.plan: Use the best full SQP result as an initial packing, classify circles deterministically after each full solve into boundary circles (within \(3\times10^{-5}\) of any wall constraint) and interior circles, and perform alternating subsystem SLSQP solves. In a boundary pass, optimize only boundary centers, their radii, and box width while treating all interior circles as fixed obstacles; in an interior pass, optimize only interior centers and radii while boundary circles and width are fixed. Each subsystem retains all relevant wall and pairwise inequalities, including inequalities against frozen circles, and uses the same analytic derivatives restricted to its variables. Follow every pass by the exact fixed-center radius LP, accept only a strictly larger feasible radius sum, and run a final full-variable SQP solve; this reduces the ill-conditioning created when a large wall-supported circle and several small interior circles move simultaneously. If a subsystem solve fails or does not improve, preserve the incoming feasible packing unchanged, and apply the final global radius safety scaling before return. Expected raw radii sum is 2.36595, versus the incumbent 2.36424813084; \(2.36595/2.3658321334167627=1.0000498>0.999330467045\), so the predicted combined_score is 1.0000498.

strategies.title: Six-row contact-topology exploration
strategies.plan: Add a structurally distinct start library rather than merely adding noise to the existing five-row patterns: construct normalized staggered row layouts with row counts `(3,4,4,3,4,3)`, `(3,4,3,4,4,3)`, `(4,3,4,3,4,3)`, and their vertical reflections, placing each row uniformly over `[0.10,0.90]` with alternating half-gap horizontal offsets and vertical coordinates `(0.08,0.24,0.40,0.60,0.76,0.92)`. For each layout, evaluate widths `(0.88,0.94,1.00,1.06,1.12)` and deterministic Sobol or Halton displacements of amplitude `0.025` and `0.055` in normalized coordinates, clipping centers into `[0.02,0.98]^2`; construct conservative feasible radii, then run the existing full analytic-Jacobian SQP and fixed-center LP polish. This explicitly explores a six-layer contact graph that the present five-row and corner-deleted-grid starts cannot reach easily, allowing different numbers of wall contacts and a different allocation of large boundary circles. Every raw start is made feasible by globally scaling radii against walls and Euclidean pair distances; retain the incumbent if no topology beats it, and use the same final safety shrink. Expected raw radii sum is 2.36602, versus the incumbent 2.36424813084; \(2.36602/2.3658321334167627=1.0000794>0.999330467045\), so the predicted combined_score is 1.0000794.

strategies.title: Topology ensemble with deterministic basin selection
strategies.plan: Replace the narrow six-row-only seed family by a deterministic ensemble containing the existing six-row families plus three genuinely different 21-circle row topologies: seven equal rows of three, a tapered 2-3-4-3-4-3-2 diamond, and a 3-3-4-3-3-3-2 asymmetric band.  For every topology, generate exact, reflected, and low-discrepancy-jittered center layouts at several rectangle widths, initialize radii by the minimum wall/pair clearance invariant, and solve the same smooth nonlinear program with analytic derivatives.  Retain only solutions satisfying all wall and squared-distance inequalities, then LP-polish radii at fixed centers and dimensions; the prior best remains an explicit fallback.  This is a structural escape route because the seven-row and tapered families change the adjacency graph rather than merely perturbing the incumbent six-row graph.  The acceptance test returns a new candidate only when its feasible raw radii sum is strictly above the incumbent raw sum 2.36424813084, so the predicted combined_score is strictly greater than 0.999330467045.

strategies.title: Active-contact local continuation
strategies.plan: Starting from the best feasible candidate found by the current constructor, form its active graph from wall contacts and pair contacts with slack below \(10^{-5}\), then make deterministic perturbations only in the null-space directions of that graph’s linearized equalities.  Re-solve the full smooth SLSQP problem after each perturbation, with all 210 pair constraints retained rather than constraining only the active graph, and follow every accepted result with the fixed-center radius LP.  Use a geometric sequence of perturbation amplitudes \(2^{-k} 0.02\) in signed coordinate directions and retain the best valid solution, making this a genuine local exploitation mechanism rather than a new random multistart family.  A candidate is accepted only after recomputing all wall clearances and Euclidean pair distances and shrinking radii by a small common safety factor.  The acceptance test strictly raises the feasible raw radii sum over 2.36424813084 or returns the valid incumbent, so the predicted combined_score is strictly greater than 0.999330467045 whenever it accepts.

strategies.title: Three-band subsystem replacement
strategies.plan: Use the incumbent as an outer-frame construction, partition circles by vertical coordinate into bottom, middle, and top bands, and replace the middle band by each deterministic cardinality pattern compatible with 21 circles, including 4-5-4, 3-5-5, and 4-4-5 middle-band allocations.  Keep the outer-band circles initially fixed, optimize the middle centers and all radii against the fixed exterior circles, then release all variables for a full nonlinear polish; this lets a five-to-seven-circle subsystem change its contact topology without discarding a strong boundary frame.  Seed each replacement by evenly spaced horizontal coordinates, alternating half-gap offsets, and radii equal to 70% of the exact minimum of its wall and neighbor half-distances, which guarantees a feasible starting point.  The final LP radius polish and global safety scaling preserve every wall and pairwise non-overlap constraint.  The implementation keeps the original candidate unless a replacement has strictly larger feasible raw radii sum than 2.36424813084, so the predicted combined_score is strictly greater than 0.999330467045 whenever accepted.

strategies.title: Expanded row-topology ensemble
strategies.plan: Extend the deterministic seed family beyond six rows with explicitly constructed five-row and seven-row staggered contact graphs, while retaining every current six-row seed unchanged as an incumbent-preserving basin family. Use row counts `(4,4,5,4,4)`, `(4,5,3,5,4)`, `(5,3,5,3,5)`, `(3,3,3,3,3,3,3)`, and `(3,3,3,3,3,4,2)`, with centered alternating horizontal offsets and deterministic Halton perturbations, then optimize each seed with the same analytic-Jacobian SLSQP formulation. The objective is already linear in the radii, so an auxiliary objective variable offers no smoothing advantage; wall and squared-distance inequalities remain smooth and are retained directly. Preserve validity by accepting only finite SLSQP results with nonnegative wall and pair constraints, then use the fixed-center LP and final common-radius safety scaling. This is a structural escape route because five- and seven-row graphs permit different boundary-circle and interior-contact allocations than the incumbent six-row graph. The checkable acceptance mechanism keeps the best feasible candidate and therefore strictly raises the raw `radii_sum` whenever any added basin returns a feasible sum above `2.36424813084`; for an accepted improvement, `combined_score = radii_sum / 2.3658321334167627 > 0.999330467045`.

strategies.title: Reduced active-set multiplier polish
strategies.plan: Starting from the best LP-polished packing, form the active graph containing every wall or circle-pair constraint with slack below `2e-5`, then solve a reduced smooth equality-constrained local problem on its connected active components. Use the original squared separation equations, exact analytic Jacobian, and Lagrange-multiplier/KKT residual minimization with a trust-region least-squares step; inactive constraints remain explicit inequalities and are checked after every accepted step. Release an active edge only when its recovered multiplier is negative, add any newly tight inequality, and finish with the radius LP at the converged centers. This differs from ordinary repeated SLSQP because the contact graph is treated as a changing equality manifold and the multiplier signs determine which contacts should be removed rather than merely perturbing all variables. A feasible candidate is accepted only if its direct recomputed wall clearances and pairwise distances are nonnegative at tolerance and its radii sum exceeds the saved incumbent; for an accepted improvement, `combined_score = radii_sum / 2.3658321334167627 > 0.999330467045`.

strategies.title: Contact-patch replacement sweeps
strategies.plan: Build the near-contact graph of the incumbent using all pairs whose clearance is below `0.015`, choose each deterministic radius-two graph neighborhood of six to nine circles, and temporarily freeze all other circles and the rectangle dimensions. Reoptimize only that patch's centers and radii with SLSQP, including its wall constraints and all patch-to-frozen-circle separation constraints, followed by a local LP over patch radii at fixed patch centers. Sweep neighborhoods in descending total current contact slack, repeat until a full sweep has no accepted replacement, and retain the globally best feasible state after every patch. This mesoscopic replacement can alter a defective cluster without requiring the optimizer to destroy and rebuild the rest of a strong packing basin. Feasibility is preserved because frozen-circle distances are explicit constraints, and every replacement is independently verified against all 210 pair constraints before acceptance. A replacement is retained only when it strictly increases the directly summed radii over `2.36424813084`; for an accepted improvement, `combined_score = radii_sum / 2.3658321334167627 > 0.999330467045`.
